acceptance_criteria.criterion: runScript() returns a numeric exit code (not void, not process.exit())
runLongScript() returns an object with child (ChildProcess) and exitCode (Promise<number>)
sh() returns exit code 0 on success, non-zero on failure
sh() defaults to shell: true on Windows
IS_WIN and NPM are exported and correct for the runtime platform
No function in the runners module calls process.exit()

summary: Implemented src/runners.ts with IS_WIN, NPM constants and runScript(), runLongScript(), sh() functions.
runScript() uses spawnSync with stdio:inherit, returns numeric exit code (null coalesces to 1), no process.exit().
runLongScript() uses spawn, returns { child: ChildProcess, exitCode: Promise<number> }. Promise resolves from 'exit' event or 1 on 'error'.
sh() uses spawnSync, defaults shell to IS_WIN (true on Windows), merges caller options, returns exit code.
Created tests/runners.test.ts with 20 tests covering all 7 acceptance criteria using vi.mock factory (required for ESM built-in modules).
All 59 tests pass (20 new + 39 pre-existing). TypeScript typecheck passes with no errors.

comments.note: Note for QA: vi.mock with factory was required for node:child_process — ESM namespace objects are non-configurable, so vi.spyOn does not work on Node built-ins. The approach (module-level mock fns + vi.mock factory) is the correct Vitest pattern for ESM built-ins.
src/runners.ts: No process.exit() in code paths. runScript/sh use spawnSync; runLongScript uses spawn + Promise. All three are clean and straightforward.

summary: All 7 acceptance criteria verified. 75/75 tests pass (20 new in runners.test.ts + 55 pre-existing). TypeScript typecheck clean.
AC1: runScript() uses spawnSync + null-coalesce (status ?? 1) — never calls process.exit(). Tests verify 0, non-zero, and null-signal cases.
AC2: runLongScript() returns {child, exitCode: Promise<number>}. Tests cover normal exit, null exit (→ 1), and error event (→ 1).
AC3-AC4: sh() returns correct exit codes; defaults shell to IS_WIN; caller can override. Option merging verified by mock capture.
AC5: IS_WIN and NPM derived from process.platform at module load — runtime-accurate by construction.

AC7: npm run typecheck passes with no errors.

comments.note: tests/runners.test.ts: Static process.exit() check strips single-line comments (// and *) but not block comments (/* ... */). A process.exit() inside a block comment would pass undetected. Low risk given codebase style, but the regex could be extended to strip /* */ blocks for robustness.

runLongScript() registers both 'exit' and 'error' handlers on the child. If both fire, the Promise resolves on first settlement (correct per Promise spec). No double-resolution issue — behavior is sound.
vi.mock factory pattern for node:child_process is the correct Vitest/ESM approach. No issues — mock isolation is clean across all describe blocks using afterEach mockReset.

summary: Reviewed src/runners.ts, src/types.ts, tests/runners.test.ts, and package.json. 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium findings. Security sign-off: PASS. Implementation follows safe Node.js process-spawning patterns with no shell injection surface on non-Windows (shell defaults to false), zero production dependencies eliminating supply-chain runtime risk, and no credentials/PII handled.

comments.note: A03 (Injection) — Info: sh() defaults shell: IS_WIN (true on Windows). With shell:true active, Node.js joins the args array with spaces before passing to the OS shell, so untrusted user-controlled strings in args could permit command injection on Windows. This is a caller-responsibility concern for any future consumer that passes user input to sh(). The current codebase does not do this. Consider adding a JSDoc warning on sh() noting that args must be developer-controlled when shell is true.

A08 (Data Integrity) — Info: ScriptRunnerOptions.env replaces the entire child process environment when passed (standard Node.js spawn behaviour — not a merge). Callers who want to add env vars must explicitly spread process.env. No security concern, but a subtle footgun worth noting in the JSDoc for env.

A06 (Vulnerable Components) — Positive: Zero production dependencies. The distributed package has no runtime npm dependencies, eliminating supply-chain attack surface entirely. Dev deps (tsup, vitest, typescript, @types/node) are all on current major versions with no known advisories.

summary: WP-005 passes code review. src/runners.ts is well-structured and maintainable: three narrowly-scoped functions with clean JSDoc, correct null-coalescing for exit codes, proper async pattern for runLongScript (spawn + Promise via 'exit'/'error' events), and safe option-merging (spread after defaults allows correct overrides). types.ts ScriptRunnerOptions is appropriately defined in the types module and reused across all three functions (DRY). Two non-behavioral Fix-Forward JSDoc improvements applied directly: (1) security note added to sh() warning that args must be developer-controlled when shell:true; (2) ScriptRunnerOptions.env clarified to state it replaces (not merges) process.env. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: sh() JSDoc — added security note: 'When shell is true, Node.js joins args with spaces before passing to the OS shell. Never pass untrusted user input as args when the shell is enabled — doing so enables command injection.' This surfaces the Security Auditor's info finding directly at the call site.

ScriptRunnerOptions.env JSDoc — replaced 'Defaults to process.env' (misleading) with explicit replace-not-merge wording: 'When provided, this value replaces the entire environment (Node.js does not merge with process.env). To add variables while preserving the parent environment, spread explicitly: { ...process.env, MY_VAR: "value" }.' Prevents the env footgun flagged by the Security Auditor.

tests/runners.test.ts — the static process.exit() check strips // and * comment lines but not /* */ block comment spans. A process.exit() inside a block comment would pass undetected. Low risk given codebase style (JSDoc only). The regex could be extended to strip /* ... */ blocks for robustness if desired.

No over-engineering detected. All three runner functions map cleanly to their use cases: runScript (sync, inherit stdio), runLongScript (async, returns handle + promise), sh (sync with shell default for Windows .cmd scripts). The shared ScriptRunnerOptions type across all three is a good DRY decision.
